tools.name: create_owner
tools.title: Create an owner
tools.description: Creates the guest (token edm_…, issued by the account library) that opens alerts and watches, and the secret whsec_… that signs the webhooks. No sign-up. The token appears only once: keep it and send it in Authorization: Bearer in the alert and watch tools. The account library signs the token, with a limit per network and per hour, so the free allowance does not become infinite. The token has no recovery: sign in to the account and bring the lists into it (`POST /api/auth/claim`, which the account page does on sign-in) to stop depending on it. You can read `webhook_segredo` again in `GET /api/dono`. Each webhook POST carries `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` (Unix seconds) and `webhook-signature: v1,<base64>`: HMAC-SHA256 of `id.timestamp.body` with the key of your `whsec_…` (the base64 after the prefix). This is the Standard Webhooks pattern: any of its libraries can check it; reject a timestamp outside 5 minutes. After `POST /api/dono/segredo`, the previous secret still signs for 24 h (two `v1,` parts in the header).

tools.name: get_owner
tools.title: Owner
tools.description: The owner state (requires the token edm_… or the account session): account or guest, the notice e-mail, the allowance and the secret whsec_… that signs each webhook (Standard Webhooks: webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature). Each webhook POST carries `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` (Unix seconds) and `webhook-signature: v1,<base64>`: HMAC-SHA256 of `id.timestamp.body` with the key of your `whsec_…` (the base64 after the prefix). This is the Standard Webhooks pattern: any of its libraries can check it; reject a timestamp outside 5 minutes. After `POST /api/dono/segredo`, the previous secret still signs for 24 h (two `v1,` parts in the header).

tools.name: rotate_webhook_secret
tools.title: Rotate the webhook secret
tools.description: Changes the secret that signs the webhooks (requires the token edm_…). The previous secret still signs for 24 h, so you can change it without a failure window. During the 24 h, the `webhook-signature` header has two `v1,…` parts: one with the new secret and one with the previous. The receiver only needs to accept any part that matches.

tools.name: create_alert
tools.title: Create an alert
tools.description: An alert for new procurements by object terms and state (UF). Use the account session or guest token. Channels: pull, signed webhook or email. Name, organization and email recipients are optional. Two modes. By `termos`: a space requires all groups; `|` accepts alternatives within a group. By `cnpj`: known activity families produce alerts, up to `max_familias`. Unmapped activities remain in the response without an alert. The cron checks every 30 minutes. Email requires an account session and `EMAIL_ALERTAS=1`. It uses explicit recipients or the verified account email.

organizacao_id.description: Organization from `GET /api/me/empresas`. Membership and MFA are checked. Null removes the label. This does not share alert ownership.

destinatarios.description: Email recipients: `para`, `cc` and `bcc` arrays. Up to 10 distinct addresses in total. An empty `para` list uses the account email. PATCH replaces all three lists. BCC is hidden from other recipients.

filtros.description: Extra filter: modalities, municipalities, exclusions, values, open proposals and CNAEs. PATCH replaces the whole filter; {} clears it.

A CNAE outside the dictionary is listed in the response with a null family. Two modes. By `termos`: a space requires all groups; `|` accepts alternatives within a group. By `cnpj`: known activity families produce alerts, up to `max_familias`. Unmapped activities remain in the response without an alert. The cron checks every 30 minutes. Email requires an account session and `EMAIL_ALERTAS=1`. It uses explicit recipients or the verified account email.

tools.name: consulta_cnpj
tools.title: Check a company (live)
tools.description: Brazilian company record by CNPJ from the Federal Revenue (Receita Federal), with the special status when there is one (bankruptcy, judicial recovery, liquidation); its sanctions (CEIS, CNEP, CEPIM, leniency agreements, TCU and the CNJ's CNIA, checked live); partners on the politically exposed persons list (CGU); tax status (federal tax debt, installment agreements, tax incentives and construction works); the Federal Revenue chronic tax debtor list (`devedorContumaz.consta`: barred from public tenders); environmental and labor risk (forced-labor list, Ibama embargoes and fines); government contracts (PNCP, federal contracts since 2013 and sales to municipalities in the state of SP, from TCE-SP) and BNDES financing; registrations with regulators and official registries (CVM, Central Bank, ANS, ANTT, ANP, ANEEL, Anatel, Anvisa, CNES, Cadastur, Ibama, ANAC and SICAF); CVM investment funds; and the address on the map (CNEFE/IBGE). Accepts the numeric and the alphanumeric CNPJ. Personal data in the record comes masked. `sancoes` has what public registries record against the whole company (the CNPJ root), updated daily: useful to vet suppliers. 10 free lookups per day per network; after that, the tool answers `free_limit` with `resets_at`.

temas.description: Comma-separated topics: dados, socios, sancoes, fiscal, divida, obras, trabalho, ibama, contratos, pep, vendas, campanhas, prefeituras, sicaf, aeronaves, fundos, rntrc, bndes, registros; todos. Omit for the full record. Basic company data always stays. Unrequested blocks are omitted; null means unchecked. Personal data remains masked.

tools.name: consulta_cep
tools.title: Check a CEP
tools.description: Addresses at a CEP (Brazilian postal code) with coordinates (CNEFE/IBGE) and the companies registered there. Returns up to 20 addresses and up to 20 companies; the total number of addresses is in `pontos_total`. 10 free lookups per day per network; after that, the tool answers `free_limit` with `resets_at`.
